Step 6
Since the P-value = 0.0076 is less than
α

There is statistical evidence to conclude that
the proportion of students who enrolled
directly in college is no longer 66%. Since the

the proportion has declined.
The final example of this section covers how to conduct a hypothesis test for proportions with raw data.
Using STATBELT or another software package you can manage this easily. If you are using a
calculator or calculator app, you may have to summarize the data yourself first, then follow the process
we have been using. Some apps will allow you to type in the data manually, but that is likely more work
than summarizing it yourself first. The best option is to use technology to conduct the test.
STATBELT Utility- Hypothesis Testing Proportions for Raw Data
To conduct a hypothesis test for a proportion using STATBELT Utility and raw data, follow the path:
Tests → Inference for Proportions → One sample → Hypothesis test.
Under “Where is the data?” choose “Column data from the main spreadsheet,” then choose the
column that contains the data.
Under “Count as a success,” choose the outcome you want to count as a success. STATBELT lists
each outcome exactly as it is typed in the column, so “Vaccinated” and “vaccinated” would be listed
as two different outcomes.
Type the proportion p from the null hypothesis into “Hypothesized proportion p₀.”
Under “Type of test,” choose Left-tailed (<), Right-tailed (>), or Two-tailed (≠).
Type the significance level α. The results appear as soon as you type.
The output from STATBELT will include the sample proportion, the test statistic, and the P-Value.
Example 8
: Hypothesis Testing Proportions from Raw Data
According to the Center for Disease Control, as of July 2022, 78% of Americans had received at least one
dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. A student survey from December 2021 asked individuals to identify
themselves as “Vaccinated” or “Unvaccinated” against COVID-19. The raw data had 148 observations as
shown in
Table 2
. You can copy the
vaccination data
. Test the hypothesis that the rate of vaccination was
significantly lower in December 2021 than it was in July 2022 at the 0.05 significance level.
Solution
In this problem we are asked to test whether the rates of vaccination was lower in December 2021
than it was in July 2022. We will apply the same six-step process, but this time we will not have
summary statistics.
Step 1
We can identify the claim that as of July, 78% of Americans have received at least one dose of
a COVID-19 vaccine. The final sentence asks us to test the hypothesis that the rate of
vaccinations was lower in December 2021, based on the student survey data. So, the null
hypothesis is
